name: Emotional Arc Trajectory
description: Maps the progression of sentiment and emotional intensity throughout a text. AI models are safety-aligned to remain neutral, helpful, and polite, resulting in mechanically 'flat' or unnaturally stable emotional arcs.
mechanism: Human storytelling and persuasive writing naturally follow established 'emotional arcs' (e.g., 'Man in Hole': a fall into despair followed by a triumphant rise, or 'Icarus': a steady rise followed by a catastrophic fall). Human writers use sharp spikes in emotional valence to build tension, climax, and catharsis. Large Language Models, however, are heavily filtered through RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) to be perpetually harmless, objective, and helpful. Consequently, AI struggles to synthesize genuine emotional volatility. Even when explicitly prompted to write a 'dramatic' or 'angry' story, the AI's emotional trajectory typically reverts to a baseline of moderate positivity or sterile neutrality. This method slices the text into chronological segments (e.g., beginning, middle, end) and maps the sentiment polarity and emotional intensity of each segment to create a trajectory line. A text that maintains a suspiciously flat, unwavering emotional valence—lacking the deep valleys of negativity or the sharp peaks of high-arousal emotion typical of human expression—strongly indicates an artificial, safety-aligned origin.
useCase: Detecting AI generation in creative writing, personal essays, op-eds, and reviews where the absence of natural emotional peaks and valleys reveals a machine's sanitized, risk-averse programming.
strengths:
• Highly effective at detecting AI in creative or personal genres where emotional fluctuation is expected.
• Exposes the underlying RLHF (safety training) of commercial models, which is virtually impossible for a standard user to turn off entirely.
• Difficult to bypass with simple prompts, as AI models stubbornly resist sustaining intense negative emotions over long passages.
limitations:
• Prone to false positives on naturally 'flat' human writing, such as technical manuals, academic research papers, and objective news reports.
• Requires a longer text sample to plot a meaningful trajectory; cannot correctly assess the 'arc' of a single paragraph.
• Sentiment analysis models tracking the arc may misinterpret complex human sarcasms or subtle emotional nuances.
parameters:
Analysis: Chronological Segmentation & Valence/Arousal Scoring
Metric: Emotional Volatility Variance (Peak-to-Trough Amplitude)
Output: 0-100 Arc Flatness (Sterile Neutrality) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% on narrative and persuasive texts. It is a powerful profiling tool that detects the behavioral 'personality' of safety-aligned AI models.

references.title: Reagan, A. J. et al. (2016). The emotional arcs of stories are dominated by six basic shapes. EPJ Data Science.
Wang, Y. et al. (2023). Is ChatGPT a Good Sentiment Analyzer? A Preliminary Study. arXiv.
